title: The Impact of AI on Productivity and Code (IEEE Software guest editors' introduction, Yedida, Menzies, Novielli, Jul/Aug 2026)

edges.target: Menzies retrospective on defect predictors / need for baselines
edges.ref: T. Menzies, "Retrospective: Data mining static code attributes to learn defect predictors," IEEE TSE, vol. 51, no. 3, pp. 858-863, 2025
edges.evidence: only 13/229 ~ 5% of those papers compared LLMs to other approaches. This is a methodological error since other methods can produce results that are better and/or faster.6

edges.target: Kocaguneli et al., Distributed development considered harmful? (Microsoft auto-generated code)
edges.ref: E. Kocaguneli, T. Zimmermann, C. Bird, N. Nagappan, T. Menzies, "Distributed development considered harmful?" ICSE 2013, pp. 882-890
edges.evidence: it is known that Microsoft has been automatically generating its code, via traditional build systems, for decades.5

not_reuse_examples: [2] Zheng et al. MultiCodeBench and [11] Zhuo et al. BigCodeBench: benchmark results summarized as background; the editorial does not run or use these benchmarks.
[4] Alshahwan et al. TestGen-LLM at Meta: industrial results quoted as evidence of benefits; tool not executed or built upon.
[13] Orel et al. CoDet-M4 and [14] He et al. LLM-as-judge: survey-style background on detection/evaluation, not adopted as a method.
A1-A6 special-issue articles: summarized as the issue's contents, not reused.
notes: Guest editors' introduction to a special issue: no experiments, no datasets, no tools run; all 14 refs are background survey citations, only two low-confidence sanitycheck edges (both self-citations by Menzies) support the editorial's 'baselines are missing' argument.
